ravqc.purpose: RAVQ calibrated (C2 = our own WAM VQ framework): (1) the reader metric M on the imagined future, estimated once from the BF16 model, is the calibration target of the future part; (4) only QTIP's own shared parameters are calibrated (the decode LUT tied per module and bit width, the row / column scales SV / SU, the output biases), on A + lam_M Z_M + beta K, starting from the uncalibrated RAVQ arms (QTIP rounding under the C1 module budget, results/ravq). C1 motivates each piece: the action expert reads the future through a narrow, context-shared channel (the reader), so the future error that matters is the one in that channel (M); shared parameters carry corrections that generalize, per-layer free parameters memorize C80 (fwld1, lowrank gate).

metric.definition: M_c = J_R(z_T)^T diag(h/2) J_R(z_T): the Gauss-Newton matrix of K at the BF16 point (BF16 reader at the teacher future of context c, h = soft-bin KL curvature at the teacher action, first10 x 6 motor), probed by c = J_R^T (eps sqrt(h/2)), eps Rademacher; frames 1: of the future only (frame 0 is the clamped observation)
metric.normalization: each context to unit trace (probe vectors divided by sqrt(P tr_c)), then the mean: every context weighs the same (the GN masses of the earlier phases had context ESS 1-26 of 80)
metric.form: M_R = E^T diag(lam) E + diag(d_res) from the normalized probes (top-r eigenpairs, residual diagonal); M = (1 - rho) (D / tr M_R) M_R + rho I, so tr M = D and M = I gives the plain NMSE back
metric.Z_M: Z_M = (z_S - z_T)^T M (z_S - z_T) / |z_T|^2 over frames 1:, the NMSE in the reader metric
metric.lam_rule: lam_M = lambda x mean_C80(Z) / mean_C80(Z_M) of the arm at its start (RAVQU): lam_M Z_M carries the same initial loss mass as lambda Z did in Q0's A + lambda Z
metric.stability: split by case parity: Pearson correlation of the two halves' diagonals, mean squared cosine between the halves' top-r subspaces; reported, not gated

families.lut: per (role, K) group one [512, 2] offset on QTIP's decode table (HYB, quantlut_sym): every pair coded with entry k of a layer in the group moves by (sign * d_k0, d_k1) in units of the layer's Wscale, in the rotated domain; one table per group = a codebook shared by all layers of a module at one bit width
families.row: per output row a log-scale s (folds into QTIP's SV, stored FP32 per row: 0 extra bits)
families.col: per input column a log-scale t (folds into QTIP's SU, stored BF16 per column: 0 extra bits)
families.bias: per output channel an additive offset on layers that have a bias (folds into the bias: 0 extra bits)
families.excluded: interfaces (BF16 for every arm) and the time-conditioning tables (exact): not calibrated
families.weight: W' = bf16(e^s * (W_q + dW_lut) * e^t), dW_lut = diag(SV) H_m^T (Wscale D(d)) H_n diag(SU); b' = bf16(b + db); at zero parameters W' = W_q bitwise

loss.objective: A + lam_M Z_M + beta K: A first10 x 6 motor MSE of the student's executed action, Z_M on the student's future, K the frozen BF16 reader on the student's future (biases reset to the originals inside the reader)

training.schedule: the loss-pair C80 schedule: 8 batches of 10 contexts, sampler seed index 0 (Q0's budget)
training.update: one gradient step in relative units, tune.json's rule: u = row / column log-scale s_r, t_c as they are; a bias element relative to its row's output scale, u_i = db_i / (|W_r| rms(x)); a table entry relative to the table's rms, u_k = d_k / rms(tlut); delta u = -eta g_u / max|g_u| over every element of every family, so the element with the largest relative gradient moves eta and the rest in proportion
training.step_rule: batch 1 at the start: predicted first-order decrease eta sum g_u^2 / max|g_u| against the realized decrease on the same batch; the largest eta with realized >= min_realized_fraction x predicted; that step is update 1; none passing -> the arm is not trained
training.step_grid_basis: tune.json's grid (0.005 ... 0.05, QTIP chose 0.01 with realized 0.57 of predicted in 26059212) plus 0.0025: a relative change under half a BF16 spacing (~0.2%) of a folded weight rounds back to the same value, so smaller steps realize only through the largest elements

update_rule_change.old_update: per tensor (a layer's row, column or bias vector; a group's table) a relative step in metric coordinates: delta u = -eta ref g_u / |g_u|, u the coordinates whose Euclidean norm is the Frobenius norm of the weight change (row: s_r |W_r|, column: t_c |W^c|, table: d_k sqrt(sum_layers Wscale^2 n_k), bias: db itself), ref = |W|_F (table: sqrt of the group's sum |W|^2, bias: |W|_F sqrt(E|x|^2 / n))
update_rule_change.why: with the per-tensor normalized step every one of ~1800 tensors moved eta ref regardless of its gradient, i.e. a sign-like step that concentrates each tensor's budget on its largest rows / columns (text_embedding.0 column scales ~4% at eta 0.000625); the loss rose at every grid point (W2 total 0.00169 -> 0.00235 at the smallest, predicted decrease 7x the loss itself), both arms untrained. tune.json 26057132 saw the same with Adam's sign step (+34-69%) and fixed it with this max-normalized gradient step
update_rule_change.archived: results/ravqc/<arm>/{arm,step}.r0_26073904.json; fit_before and the zm files are rule-independent and reused

codes.need: every (layer, K) the base arms' sources.json gives a QTIP K (text, video body, action body)
codes.K1_K4: results/ravq/qtip_K<k>/codes: the stored trellis -> 16-bit states -> (LUT entry, sign) per pair (quantlut_sym hash)
codes.K2_K3: the A16 baselines stored dense weights only; nearest-candidate recovery from the BF16 weight misreads ~0.2% of the pairs (CPU test 26073382: sign twins of table entries near t0 = 0 lie within the BF16 noise), so each layer is requantized with ravq_qtip (the port, same seed and H_U) and its trellis taken; it must reproduce the stored weight bit for bit, otherwise the fresh QTIP rounding becomes that layer's start (counted and reported)
codes.check: every layer: bf16(inverse incoherence of Wscale x D(codes)) equals the arm's stored weight bit for bit

reading.primary: held-out 40x2 of RAVQC_Wb against RAVQU_Wb (same bits): future NMSE, Z_M, mixed loss, first10 motor, gripper; and against the fair reference QTIP_WbI and the A16 host QTIP_Wb
reading.loop: both calibrated arms run LIBERO-Plus 280, paired with QTIP_Wb (A16), RAVQU_Wb and QTIP_WbI where those loops exist

allocation_job.time_basis: codes: 1208 (layer, K) items; K = 1 / 4 (604) decode their stored trellis; K = 2 / 3 (860 layers minus overlap) are requantized: the baselines' QTIP W2 / W3 took 1.86 / 1.88 GPU-h for all 614 layers, the needed share ~87% / 85% -> ~3.2 GPU-h, ~50 min on 4 GPUs; metric: 80 contexts x (BF16 reader read + 4 probe VJPs) ~5 s -> ~2 min per GPU

calib_job.time_basis: per arm and GPU: fit before 80 queries (~3 min); step check: 1 gradient batch (10 x (staged queries + reader + grad replay ~30 s + table reduction ~50 s)) ~14 min + 4 grid evaluations x 10 (query + reader) ~3 min; 7 more updates ~95 min; deploy + fit after + held-out 80 x 4 s ~12 min: ~2.2 h; zm 6 arms x 80 queries / 2 GPUs ~8 min

loop_job.time_basis: 8 workers (2 per GPU) on one episode queue, ~80 s per episode: 280 / 8 x 80 s ~47 min per arm plus startup
